# Cūḷaassapura Sutta (MN 40 (PTS MN i 281))

**ID:** MN 40 (PTS MN i 281)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷaassapura Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Shorter Discourse at Assapura
**PTS:** MN i 281
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/mn40

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷaassapura Sutta* ("The Shorter Discourse at Assapura", MN 40) is the fortieth discourse in the *Majjhimanikāya* [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Delivered at Assapura, it functions as a companion piece to the preceding *Mahāassapura Sutta* (MN 39) [Humphreys 1956; Rogell 2003]. The sutta defines "the way proper to the recluse" (*samaṇa*), asserting that monastic designation and ascetic status are not earned merely through external trappings, formal requisites (such as wearing the patchwork robe), or external bodily austerities (such as nakedness or ceremonial bathing) [SuttaCentral; Durham 2004; Bronkhorst 1998; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. Instead, genuine asceticism requires inward purification from unwholesome mental defilements, specifically including ill-will and other corruptions of the mind [Durham 2004; Anālayo; Rogell 2003]. When a practitioner observes freedom from these unwholesome states, gladness and joy arise, leading successively to bodily tranquility, happiness, and meditative concentration [Shaw 2006], with the text also incorporating the practice of the four divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*) [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995].

A full parallel to the discourse is preserved in the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 183), an alignment also corroborated by DharmaNexus matching data with the *Zhong ahan jing* (T 26) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral also records a reference to the discourse in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.9) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects 834 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 75 texts; its opening section is closely shared with the *Mahāassapura Sutta* (MN 39 §1.1–2.7), while subsequent passages concerning gladness, tranquility, and the divine abodes exhibit substantial reuse with sections of the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (AN 4, AN 5, AN 10, AN 3), the *Maghadeva Sutta* (MN 83), and the *Gāmaṇi Saṁyutta* (SN 42) [DharmaNexus]. In modern scholarship, its ascetic formulations have been compared with related praxis sections in the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* [Cheung 2013], and complete English translations have been produced by I.B. Horner, Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi, and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995].
